questions.q: Two air conditioners of the same size cost the same. One has 2 BEE stars and the other has 4. Rohini's family wants the lower electricity bill. What should they choose, and why?
questions.a: More BEE stars indicate that the appliance uses less energy and electricity, so the 4-star one gives a lower bill. More stars do not mean more cooling or a higher price.
o: The 4-star one, since more stars means less electricity
The 2-star one, since fewer stars means less electricity
The 4-star one, since more stars means more cooling
The 2-star one, since it is certainly cheaper

questions.q:
Match each mark in Column A with what it is used for, in Column B.
Column A: 1. FSSAI  2. ISI  3. AGMARK  4. BEE Star
Column B: a. energy efficiency of TVs, laptops and air conditioners  b. agricultural products such as pulses and honey  c. food that has been tested and is safe to consume  d. electrical appliances, construction materials, tyres and paper
questions.a: FSSAI - food tested and safe; ISI - appliances, construction materials, tyres, paper; AGMARK - agricultural products; BEE Star - energy efficiency. The wrong pairings swap ISI with BEE or FSSAI with AGMARK.

questions.q: A builder in Nagpur wants to buy cement, and an auto-rickshaw owner wants new tyres. Which certification mark would both look for?
questions.a: The ISI mark, issued by BIS, is generally present on construction materials and automotive tyres. AGMARK is for farm products, FSSAI for food and BEE stars for energy use of appliances.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A packet of gram flour shows its date of manufacture and its best before date.
Reason (R): The FSSAI logo on a food packet indicates that the food has been tested by the government.
Choose the correct option.
questions.a: Both statements are true, but the FSSAI logo is about testing for safety and says nothing about why dates appear on a label, so R does not explain A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.q:
Read the statements about judging quality.
1. A BEE Star rating with more stars means that the appliance uses more electricity.
2. AGMARK is the certification mark printed on TVs and laptops.
3. The reputation of a product can be built through word of mouth.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is reversed: more stars mean less electricity. Statement 2 is false: AGMARK is for agricultural products, while BEE stars appear on TVs and laptops.

questions.q: Two air conditioners are used through the year. One uses 1,200 units of electricity a year and the other uses 900 units a year, and a unit costs Rs 8. (a) Find the yearly electricity bill for each. (b) Which one is likely to carry more BEE stars, and how much does the family save each year with it?
questions.a: (a) 1,200 x 8 = Rs 9,600 and 900 x 8 = Rs 7,200. (b) The one using 900 units, since more stars mean less electricity; it saves 9,600 - 7,200 = Rs 2,400 a year.
s: Part (a): Rs 9,600 and Rs 7,200
Part (b): the 900-unit one has more stars; saving of Rs 2,400

questions.q: (a) What does BEE stand for? (b) A family chooses a 5-star appliance over a 2-star one. State one gain for the family and one for the environment.
questions.a: (a) Bureau of Energy Efficiency. (b) More stars indicate the appliance uses less energy and electricity, so the family's electricity bill is lower, and less energy is used, which is good for the environment.
s: Part (a): Bureau of Energy Efficiency
Part (b): lower bill for the family and less energy used for the environment

questions.q: Name any four pieces of information that the chapter shows on the label of a packet of gram flour.
questions.a: Any four of: net quantity, best before date, date of manufacture, MRP, manufacturer's name and address, nutrition facts panel, batch number, allergen declaration, FSSAI mark and licence number, ingredients list.
s: Two correct items
Two more correct items

questions.q: Differentiate between the FSSAI mark and the ISI mark by saying what each guarantees and the kind of goods that carry it.
questions.a: FSSAI shows that food has been tested by the government and is safe to consume, so it is on food packets and cartons. The ISI mark, issued by BIS, ensures quality and safe use of goods like electrical appliances, construction materials, tyres and paper.
s: FSSAI: tested and safe food, on food packets
ISI: quality and safe use, on appliances, construction materials, tyres and paper

questions.q: Apart from certification marks, name two other ways in which a consumer can judge whether to buy a product, and say where each is used.
questions.a: Reputation built by word of mouth, such as buying what friends or relatives suggest; and online reviews and feedback from other consumers, used while shopping online.
s: Word of mouth or reputation, with how it is used
Online reviews, used when shopping online

questions.q: A shopkeeper says, 'Buy this 5-star TV instead of the 3-star one and you will save Rs 3,000 on electricity every year.' The 3-star TV uses 250 units a year, the 5-star TV uses 150 units a year, and a unit costs Rs 8. Show that his claim cannot be correct. What does the chapter say a higher star rating does to the bill?
questions.a: 3-star bill: 250 x 8 = Rs 2,000. 5-star bill: 150 x 8 = Rs 1,200. The yearly saving is only Rs 800, so Rs 3,000 is impossible. The chapter says more stars mean the appliance uses less electricity, so the bill is smaller, but not by the amount he says.
s: Both yearly bills worked out
Saving of Rs 800 shown to be less than Rs 3,000
Higher stars mean less electricity and a lower bill

questions.q: Asha says, 'If a packet has the FSSAI logo and good online reviews, I can trust it. But if a product has no certification mark, it must be unsafe.' Do you agree fully, partly or not at all? Give reasons from the chapter.
questions.a: Partly. The first half is supported: the FSSAI symbol indicates that the food has been tested by the government and is safe to consume, and online reviews and feedback from other consumers help us decide whether to buy. The second half goes beyond the chapter: it says certification confirms that a product fulfils minimum quality standards, but it does not say that every unmarked product is unsafe. An absent mark means only that there is nothing to confirm quality, so the buyer should look for other evidence.
s: Verdict: agrees only partly
Accepts FSSAI as tested and safe, and reviews as a help
Rejects 'must be unsafe': the chapter does not say so, an absent mark means only no confirmation

questions.q: A notice board in your colony needs a shopping tip headed 'Look for the mark'. Write three lines, one each for a packet of pulses, a refrigerator and a car tyre, naming the mark a buyer should look for and what it tells the buyer.
questions.a: Any suitable tip, e.g. pulses: look for AGMARK, the certification mark for agricultural products (FSSAI shows food tested and safe); refrigerator: look for the BEE Star rating, since more stars mean less electricity (an ISI mark is also found on electrical appliances); car tyre: look for the ISI mark issued by BIS, which ensures quality and safe use. Each line must name a correct mark and what it tells the buyer.
s: Pulses with AGMARK or FSSAI and what it tells
Refrigerator with BEE Star rating or ISI and what it tells
Car tyre with the ISI mark and what it tells

questions.q: Your parent asks you to buy a 1 kg packet of gram flour, and your sister wants to buy a new laptop. Explain how each of you can judge quality, naming the labels and marks that would help, and one other source of information for the laptop.
questions.a: For the gram flour: read the label for net quantity, date of manufacture and best before date, MRP, ingredients, batch number, allergen declaration and the manufacturer's name; look for the FSSAI mark and licence number, showing the food is tested and safe. For the laptop: look for the ISI mark, issued by BIS, where applicable, and the BEE Star rating; more stars means less electricity. Other sources are word of mouth from friends and relatives, and online reviews and feedback from other consumers.
s: Label details on the gram flour packet
FSSAI as the mark of tested, safe food
ISI mark and BIS for the appliance
BEE Star rating and what more stars mean
Word of mouth or online reviews

questions.q: Compare certification marks with online reviews and word of mouth as ways of judging quality. Analyse the strengths of each and say which a consumer should depend on when buying medicine or food for the family.
questions.a: Certification marks like FSSAI, ISI and AGMARK are given by government agencies and confirm that a product meets minimum quality standards, so they are dependable for safety. Online reviews and word of mouth come from other buyers and build a product's reputation, helping a buyer decide whether to buy, but they are opinions and are not tested by an agency. For food and medicine, where health is involved, the family should rely first on the certification marks and then use reviews and word of mouth as support. The point that reviews are only opinions is reasoning, not a statement in the chapter.
s: Certification marks given by government agencies
They confirm minimum quality standards
Reviews and word of mouth shape reputation
Difference in reliability
A reasoned choice for food or medicine

questions.q:
A school kitchen wants 20 jars of honey of 500 g each. Three online sellers offer:
Seller X: Rs 300 a jar, shows FSSAI and AGMARK marks, rating 4.1 stars from 850 reviews.
Seller Y: Rs 240 a jar, shows no certification mark, rating 4.8 stars from 9 reviews.
Seller Z: Rs 280 a jar, shows the FSSAI mark only, rating 4.4 stars from 40 reviews.
(a) Which details in the offers come from government agencies and which from other consumers?
(b) What does the FSSAI mark, carried by X and Z, show?
(c) How much more would the school pay for 20 jars from X than from Y?
(d) Which seller would you choose for the school kitchen? Decide, and give one point from marks and one from reviews.
questions.a: (a) The FSSAI and AGMARK marks come from government agencies; the star ratings and reviews are feedback from other consumers. Y shows no mark. (b) The food has been tested by the government and is safe to consume. (c) 20 x 300 = Rs 6,000 against 20 x 240 = Rs 4,800, so Rs 1,200 more. (d) A defensible choice is X: it has both FSSAI and AGMARK and the most reviews (850), so the rating is more dependable, and food safety matters for a kitchen. Choosing Z for a lower price is also acceptable if argued. Y is cheapest but has no mark and only 9 reviews, so its high rating is the least dependable.
s: Part (a): marks from government agencies; ratings and reviews from consumers
Part (b): FSSAI shows food tested and safe
Part (c): Rs 1,200
Part (d): a choice supported by marks and reviews

questions.q:
The Menon family wants a new air conditioner and has two choices. A 3-star model costs Rs 38,000 and uses 1,500 units of electricity a year. A 5-star model costs Rs 46,000 and uses 1,000 units a year. A unit costs Rs 8. The family expects to live in the house for 5 years, but it has only Rs 40,000 in savings.
(a) Which label on the air conditioner tells the family which model uses less electricity, and which model does it favour?
(b) What is the yearly electricity bill for each model, and in how many years does the 5-star model recover its extra price?
(c) Besides the family's bill, what benefit does the chapter say lower electricity use brings?
(d) Which model should the family buy? Decide, using the total cost over 5 years, the savings limit and the chapter's point.
questions.a: (a) The BEE Star rating; it favours the 5-star model, since more stars mean less electricity. (b) 1,500 x 8 = Rs 12,000 and 1,000 x 8 = Rs 8,000; the extra price Rs 8,000 is recovered in 8,000 / 4,000 = 2 years. (c) It is good for the environment. (d) Over 5 years: 3-star 38,000 + 5 x 12,000 = Rs 98,000; 5-star 46,000 + 5 x 8,000 = Rs 86,000, so the 5-star model is cheaper by Rs 12,000 and uses less energy. Buy it if the family can arrange the extra Rs 6,000 beyond its savings; if it cannot, only the 3-star model is within its savings.
s: Part (a): BEE Star rating; 5-star model
Part (b): Rs 12,000 and Rs 8,000; 2 years
Part (c): good for the environment
Part (d): decision using Rs 98,000 against Rs 86,000, the savings limit and the chapter's point
